'''Kwetiau ayam''', '''kuetiau ayam''' or sometimes '''kwetiau ayam kuah''' ([[Indonesian language|Indonesian]] for '[[Chicken (food)|chicken]] [[Shahe fen|kway teow]]') is a common [[Chinese Indonesian cuisine|Chinese Indonesian]] dish of seasoned flat [[rice noodle]]s topped with diced [[chicken meat]] (''[[wikt:ayam#Indonesian|ayam]]''). It is often described as a kwetiau version of the popular ''[[mie ayam]]'' (chicken noodles), and especially common in [[Indonesia]], and can trace its origin to [[Chinese cuisine]].<ref name="Sabrina">{{Cite web|title=Resep Kwetiaw ayam jamur bakso |author= Adis Sabrina |url=https://cookpad.com/id/resep/10826414-kwetiaw-ayam-jamur-bakso |website=Cookpad|date= 13 October 2019 |language=id|access-date=2020-05-03}}</ref> 

In Indonesia, the dish is recognized as a popular [[Chinese Indonesian cuisine|Chinese Indonesian dish]] together with [[bakso]] meatballs and ''mie ayam'', served from simple humble street-side ''[[warung]]'' to restaurants. Since the recipe is almost identical to the popular ''mie ayam'', food stalls and restaurants that serve mie ayam'' usually also offer kwetiau ayam'' and ''[[bihun]] ayam''.
